VERIFICATION ARCHITECTURE

How DAM Verifies Evidence

DAM is built to combat the unique landscape of Indian digital scams, fake government circulars, and weaponized forwards without hallucinating or producing false confidence.

RULE 1 Primary Indian Registries First

Before examining secondary reports, DAM queries authoritative primary registries:

  • Reserve Bank of India (RBI): Notifications, Master Circulars, and press releases regarding banknotes and banking regulations.
  • Press Information Bureau (PIB Fact Check): Official Government of India rebuttals of viral fake schemes.
  • TRAI & DoT: Sanchar Saathi, Chakshu, and SMS header verification rules (e.g., 6-character alpha headers vs suspicious 10-digit mobile numbers).
  • CERT-In: Vulnerability notes and malware advisories targeting Android banking APKs.

RULE 2 The Autonomous Challenger Agent

A synthesis model is never allowed to have the final word. A dedicated challenger model is run in parallel to formulate adversarial counter-arguments:

  • Are we confusing a state-level policy (e.g. Mahavitaran/BESCOM electricity notice) with a nationwide policy?
  • Has a new press release or gazette addendum been published within the last 24 hours that supersedes earlier records?
  • Is the sender utilizing typosquatting or Unicode homograph attacks?

RULE 3 Three Separate Verdicts — Never Blended

A composite number (like "78% truth") masks critical nuances. A message might contain 100% real text from an RBI circular, yet be attached to a high-risk phishing link. DAM produces three strictly separate verdicts:

  • Factual Correctness: Supported | Contradicted | Mixed | Unverified
  • Scam Risk: Low | Medium | High (with the explicit triggers that caused the rating)
  • Evidence Sufficiency: Sufficient | Partial | Insufficient

RULE 4 "Insufficient Evidence" is a First-Class Outcome

Most AI models guess when facts are scarce. In DAM, if primary sources have not published an official notification or confirmation, the verdict is explicitly recorded as Insufficient Evidence, prompting the user to await formal confirmation before taking irreversible actions.
